sections.heading: What Causes Foggy Windows and Why You Should Act Fast
sections.body: Foggy or cloudy windows occur when the hermetic seal surrounding an insulated glass unit (IGU) fails. That seal is designed to trap an inert gas — typically argon or krypton — between the two panes, providing insulation. Once the seal breaks, humid outside air infiltrates the space, condenses on the inner glass surfaces, and creates the milky or streaky appearance homeowners and property managers dread. In Arlington's humid summers and cold winters, temperature swings accelerate seal degradation, making this a common issue from the high-rise condos near Rosslyn to the older residential neighborhoods around Clarendon. Delaying repair allows moisture to etch and permanently stain the glass, meaning what could have been a simple IGU swap becomes a full-frame replacement. Acting quickly not only preserves your view but also protects your insulation value, lowers utility bills, and prevents potential mold growth in window frames caused by prolonged moisture exposure.

sections.heading: Our Foggy Window Repair Process for Arlington Properties
sections.body: Our technicians begin every foggy window repair job with a thorough on-site assessment to determine whether the insulated glass unit can be replaced within the existing frame or whether additional frame work is needed. In most cases, we can replace only the failed IGU, saving you the cost of full-window replacement. We carefully remove the damaged sealed unit, clean the frame channels, and install a new factory-sealed dual- or triple-pane unit filled with argon gas for superior thermal performance. All replacement glass is cut and sealed to manufacturer specifications. We carry a broad inventory of standard and custom sizes, allowing us to complete most Arlington jobs in a single visit. Our licensed and insured team handles everything from single-family homes in the Lyon Village neighborhood to multi-unit commercial buildings along the Ballston corridor, ensuring minimal disruption to your daily operations or household routine.

sections.heading: Energy Savings and Long-Term Benefits of Replacing Failed Seals
sections.body: Replacing a fogged insulated glass unit is one of the most cost-effective energy upgrades available to Arlington property owners. A failed seal eliminates the insulating gas layer, effectively turning your double-pane window into a single-pane unit with dramatically reduced thermal resistance. Studies show that properly sealed IGUs can reduce heat transfer by up to 50 percent compared to single-pane glass. When you factor in Arlington's climate — hot, humid summers and cold winters — the savings on HVAC costs add up quickly. Our replacement units use high-performance low-E coatings and argon fills that meet or exceed ENERGY STAR standards. Homeowners in neighborhoods like Lyon Village and Bluemont often report noticeable reductions in drafts and condensation after our repairs. For commercial clients, improved thermal performance can contribute toward green building benchmarks and reduce carbon footprint reporting obligations, adding regulatory and reputational value beyond simple utility savings.

faq.q: Can foggy window glass be repaired without replacing the entire window?
faq.a: In most cases, yes. As long as the window frame is in good condition, our technicians can replace only the failed insulated glass unit inside the existing frame. This approach is significantly more affordable than full window replacement and delivers the same results in terms of clarity and energy performance.

faq.q: How long does a foggy window repair take in Arlington?
